LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.3: Active Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Active Listening. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Respond to simple instructions in (2HRS)
2. Take turns during conversations in and out of school.
3. Take pleasure in responding to simple instructions in and out of class.
4. Enjoy taking turns in a conversation in and out of school. conversations. questions during conversations. conversations and be encouraged to view them while receiving positive feedback. others have said in a conversation. the contribution of others during conversations. 6 involved in verbal games, songs, poems and rhymes that involve turn taking. imitate demonstrations of turn taking in conversations. take turns during conversations. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, digital literacy, learning to learn

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Respond to simple instructions in (2HRS)
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to respond to simple instructions in (2HRS). Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Take turns during conversations in and out of school.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to take turns during conversations in and out of school. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Take pleasure in responding to simple instructions in and out of class.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Active Listening.
2. Explain Active Listening to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Active Listening.
4. Show that you can: Respond to simple instructions in (2HRS)
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Active Listening. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Active Listening important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

2. Take turns during conversations in and out of school.
3. Take pleasure in responding to simple instructions in and out of class.
